page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is a virtual server instance within the High Performance family, featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 180 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data reveals moderate processing capabilities alongside notable memory and storage bottlenecks. The instance achieves average performance in stress-ng single-core (2306.16) and multi-core (9232.12) tests, as well as in PassMark CPU encryption (3693.88). However, memory performance is constrained, with large-block read and write bandwidths falling into the bottom 10% at 17.9 GB/sec and 12.56 GB/sec respectively. PassMark database operations (919.74) and static web serving throughput (2.66 GB/sec) also rank in the bottom 10%, while Redis SET operations (3.94 million operations/sec) and PassMark CPU physics (578.12) register in the bottom 25%.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the low RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require dedicated hardware threads. The bundled 180 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local storage, but the poor memory bandwidth and low database benchmark scores suggest it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or high-throughput web serving. Appropriate workloads include lightweight multi-threaded applications, basic batch processing, development environments, and low-traffic utility services.
